description:
Finding: The dev-mode startup guard (auth.is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr()) is copy-pasted with different wording into three main.rs files: reader/src/main.rs lines 363-376, mail/src/main.rs lines 93-104, and imap/src/main.rs lines 76-87. Each has a distinct eprintln! string — reader says 'no users configured', mail says 'no users configured', imap says 'no authentication (no users configured, auth.required = false)' — with slightly different phrasing for the fix instructions too.

Risk: When the guard message needs updating (e.g. to mention STOA_ENV, or to add a doc URL, or to standardise the fix suggestion wording), a maintainer editing one copy has no mechanical reminder that two others exist. One copy will be missed. This has already happened: imap's message omits the second fix option that reader and mail both include.

Suggested fix: Extract a shared function — e.g. stoa_core::startup::check_dev_mode_guard(is_dev_mode: bool, listen_addr: &str, daemon_name: &str) -> Result<(), String> — in a crate visible to all three. Each main.rs calls it and passes the result to eprintln!/process::exit. The message string lives in exactly one place.
title: Dev-mode guard eprintln! strings duplicated across 3 main.rs files
